***[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]

**Six people are killed during clashes in [[Bangladesh]] as opposition demonstrators protesting [[Government of Bangladesh|government]] job quotas, which benefit pro-government families, clashes with police and pro-government supporters. **The [[Islamic State]] claims responsibility for the prior day's [[mass shooting]] at a [[Shi'ite]] mosque in [[Muscat]], [[Oman]]. This is the first attack carried out by the Islamic State in the country. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn38vx7g2e5o (BBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 25 people are killed and 17 others are injured when a bus veers off a cliff and crashes in [[Department of Ayacucho|Ayacucho Region]], [[Peru]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bus-accident-peruvian-andes-leaves-least-20-dead-2024-07-16/ (Reuters)]
*Heavy rainfall across the [[Midwestern United States]] causes a [[Dam failure|dam failure]] in [[Washington County, Illinois|Washington County]], [[Illinois]], prompting an immediate evacuation order in the nearby city of [[Nashville, Illinois|Nashville]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2024/07/16/dam-failure-nashville-illinois/74423733007/ (''USA Today'')]
*A malfunction causes an emergency shutdown of one of the four [[nuclear reactor|reactors]] at the [[Rostov Nuclear Power Plant]] in [[Rostov Oblast]], [[Russia]]. Background [[radiation]] levels are reported as normal. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/malfunction-shuts-one-four-units-russian-nuclear-power-plant-2024-07-16/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2024 European heatwaves]]
**[[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] state [[electrical grid]] operator [[Ukrenergo]] begins emergency power shutdowns in seven [[Eastern Ukraine|eastern]] and [[Central Ukraine|central]] [[Oblasts of Ukraine|oblasts]] amid a record [[Heat wave|heat wave]] and equipment failures worsened by ongoing [[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian attacks]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-starts-emergency-power-cuts-amid-record-heatwave-2024-07-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Romania]] approves the [[culling]] of 481 [[Eurasian brown bear|bear]]s in the country, after a 19-year-old woman was killed by a bear last week in the [[Carpathian Mountains]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/16/romania-to-cull-500-bears-to-curb-overpopulation-after-deadly-attack (Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Czech Republic–Ukraine relations]]
**The [[Czech Republic]] announces plans to facilitate [[Colt CZ Group]] [[Assault rifle|assault rifle]] production and the construction of an ammunition factory in [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/czech-ukraine-ammunition-factory-shmyhal/33038684.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Estonia–Russia relations]], [[Latvia–Russia relations]], [[Lithuania–Russia relations]]
**The [[Baltic states]] announce their exit from [[Russia]]'s and [[Belarus]]'s electricity grid along with plans to synchronize their grid with the [[continental Europe]] [[Synchronous grid of Continental Europe|grid]] on February 9, 2025. '''Law and crime'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip]]
***An investigation by the [[Associated Press]] and [[Israel|Israeli]] [[Investigative journalism|investigative organization]] Shomrim finds that the [[United States]] and Israel allowed [[Tax deduction|tax-deductible]] donations totaling over [[United States dollar|US$]]200,000 to multiple [[Far-right politics in Israel|Israeli far-right extremist]] groups involved in blocking and disrupting [[Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war|humanitarian aid delivery]] to the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-gaza-hamas-aid-humanitarian-nonprofit-69582d193ce270d63d5865ac0ead2df0 (AP)]
*[[Kosovo War]]
**[[War crimes in the Kosovo War]]
***The [[Kosovo Specialist Chambers]] criminal tribunal sentences former [[Kosovo Liberation Army|Liberation Army]] member Pjetër Shala to 18 years in prison for [[war crimes]] committed during the war. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/16/kosovo-war-crimes-tribunal-sentences-former-kla-member-to-18-years (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.koha.net/en/arberi/426256/pjeter-shala-denohet-me-18-vjet-burgim (''Koha Ditore'')]
*[[2024 Bangkok hotel cyanide poisoning]]
**Six [[Vietnam]]ese and [[US|American]] people are found dead at the [[Grand Hyatt Erawan Bangkok]] hotel in [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]], in a suspected [[cyanide poisoning]] incident. [https://apnews.com/article/thailand-hotel-death-poisoning-cyanide-795719445377c5be993a792aeba48586 (AP)]
*[[United States|American]] [[US Senate|senator]] [[Bob Menendez]] is found guilty on all counts, including acting as a foreign agent, in a [[Bob Menendez#2023 indictment|federal corruption trial]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/sen-bob-menendez-federal-corruption-trial-verdict/story?id=111295557 (ABC News)]
*Former governor of [[Deir ez-Zor Governorate]], [[Syria]], and director of the [[Adra Prison]] Samir Ousman al-Sheikh is arrested by the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], United States. Al-Sheikh has been accused of torturing and killing political dissidents while serving as prison director and governor. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/07/16/us/politics/syrian-official-arrested-adra-prison.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Germany|German]] authorities in four [[States of Germany|states]] search the properties of management and shareholders of the [[Far-right politics in Germany (1945–present)|right-wing extremist]] magazine ''[[Compact (German magazine)|Compact]]'', seizing assets and evidence after the magazine was banned by the [[Federal Ministry of the Interior (Germany)|interior ministry]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/germany-bans-right-wing-compact-magazine-searches-properties-four-states-2024-07-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[National Police of Paraguay|Police]] in [[Paraguay]] seize more than four tons of [[cocaine]], worth $240 million, at a river port in [[Asunción]], the largest cocaine seizure in the country's history. [https://apnews.com/article/paraguay-cocaine-trafficking-drugs-gangs-criminal-port-seizure-belgium-415cff9f6a4739f0d1cb0d728b2c7ad5 (AP)]
*[[Chinese people|Chinese]] businessman [[Guo Wengui]] is found guilty by a [[Juries in the United States|U.S. jury]] on multiple [[fraud]] charges, accused of running a [[racketeering]] enterprise from 2018 to 2023 that defrauded thousands of investors out of over $1 billion. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jul/16/guo-wengui-fraud-trial (''The Guardian'')]

*[[2024 Welsh government crisis]]
**Six weeks after losing a [[vote of no confidence]] in the [[Senedd]], [[Vaughan Gething]] [[resign]]s as [[First Minister of Wales]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/article/2024/jul/16/vaughan-gething-resigns-first-minister-wales (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Kenya Finance Bill protests]]
**[[Kenya Police|Police]] fire [[tear gas]] and [[water cannon]]s at anti-government protestors as demonstrations continue in cities across [[Kenya]], calling for the removal of [[President of Kenya|President]] [[William Ruto]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/16/new-antigovernment-protests-kick-off-in-kenya-with-calls-for-ruto-to-quit (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Roberta Metsola]] is re-elected as [[President of the European Parliament]] with the highest number of votes ever registered for a candidate in the history of the [[European Parliament]].
